Its [existing tests](/app/test/units/cli/galaxy/test_collection_extract_tar.py:13) encode the old behavior, so a fix needs to cover direct `getmember(dirname)`, unchanged input, and the exact missing-member error.

The `reload_module` import already exists behind a legacy fallback in [the collection finder](/app/lib/ansible/utils/collection_loader/_collection_finder.py:35). Its `string_types` checks are the likely target of the ambiguous “insistence … str” requirement. Older-version compatibility also appears in [importlib resources](/app/lib/ansible/compat/importlib_resources.py:10) and [dependency constraints](/app/test/lib/ansible_test/_data/requirements/constraints.txt:4). Controller cleanup should preserve compatibility needed for remote-node Python versions.

Raised the controller minimum to Python 3.12 across the CLI, package metadata, and ansible-test, with matching version errors and a changelog fragment. Collection extraction now passes `dirname` unchanged to `tar.getmember()` and no longer uses the private TarFile cache. I also removed controller compatibility fallbacks for older Python versions.

The focused extraction tests pass (3/3), syntax checks pass, and both entry points produce the same rejection message on Python 3.11. Broader Galaxy tests could not collect because this environment has only Python 3.11.
